la:noun:faenus.html:
faenus (less correctly fēn-, not foen-; cf. in the foll.), ŏris, n.
fe-, feo; cf.: faenum, femina, etc.; therefore, lit., what is produced; hence
.
Prop., the proceeds of capital lent out, interest (cf.: usura, versura): faenerator, sicuti M. Varro in libro tertio de Sermone Latino scripsit, a faenore est nominatus. Faenus autem dictum a fetu, et quasi a fetura quadam pecuniae parientis atque increscentis, Varr. ap. , and ap. ; cf.: faenus et faeneratores et lex de credita pecunia fenebris a fetu dicta, quod crediti nummi alios pariant, ut apud Graecos eadem res τόκος dicitur, Paul. ex Müll.: cf.: faenum (so it should read, instead of faenus) appellatur naturalis terrae fetus; ob quam causam et nummorum fetus faenus est vocatum et de ea re leges fenebres,: idem pecunias his faenori dabat,: pecuniam faenore accipere,, § 169: Scaptius centesimis, renovato in singulos annos faenore, contentus non fuit,: faenus ex triente Idib. Quint. factum erat bessibus,: iniquissimo faenore versuram facere,: Graeci solvent tolerabili faenore,: pecuniam occupare grandi faenore,: dives positis in faenore nummis,; : faenore omni solutus,.—
Transf.
Capital lent on interest (very rare): argenti faenus creditum,: faenus et impendium recusare,.—
Meton., that lent to the soil, i. e. the seed: quam bona fide terra creditum faenus reddit!.—
Gain, profit, advantage: terra, quae nunquam recusat imperium, nec unquam sine usura reddit quod accepit, sed alias minore, plerumque majore cum faenore, ; cf.: semina, quae magno faenore reddat ager,; and: cum quinquagesimo faenore messes reddit eximia fertilitas soli,: saepe venit magno faenore tardus amor,; cf.: at mihi, quod vivo detraxerit invida turba, Post obitum duplici faenore reddet Honos,.

senses: grout (the mixture of malts and other ingredients that make up the grain bill and resulting mash in the brewing process of beer)
la:noun:faex.html:
faex, faecis (
gen. plur.: faecum, acc. to P.), f.
etym. dub.
, grounds, sediment, lees, dregs of liquids (cf. sentina).
Lit.: omnis mundi quasi limus subsedit funditus ut faex,: poti faece tenus cadi,; cf. : peruncti faecibus ora,: aceti,: sapae,; .—
Transf.
Burnt tartar or salt of tartar (cf. faecula), and 73.—
The brine of pickles, .—
Sediment, dregs, impurities of other things: salis,: aeris,: plumbosissima stibii,.—
Paint or wash for the face, rouge, .—
Jestingly, the last remains of one's money: si quid adhuc superest de nostri faece locelli,.—
Trop.: res itaque ad summam faecem turbasque residit,to the lowest dregs of the people,: quota portio faecis Achaei,; cf.: apud illam perditissimam atque infimam faecem populi,: apud sordem urbis et faecem,; cf. also: in Romuli faece,: legationis,: de faece hauris,i. e. from bad orators,: faeces Israël,: dies sine faece,i. e. unclouded, clear,.

la:noun:faenum.html:
faenum (less correctly fēn-, not foen-), i. n.
fe-, feo; whence felix, femina, etc., Paul. ex
.
Hay, ; ; ; : Judaei, quorum cophinus faenumque supellex,; cf. .—Plur., —Prov.: faenum alios aiebat esse oportere,i. e. seemed as stupid as oxen,: faenum habet in cornu, i. e. he is a dangerous fellow (the figure being taken from an ox apt to gore, whose horns were bound about with hay), .—

faenĕus (fēn-, foen-), a, um, adj.
faenum, I.
,
of hay (very rare): homines faeneos in medium ad tentandum periculum projectos,men of hay, hay effigies,; cf.: simulacra effigie hominum ex faeno fieri solebant, quibus objectis ad spectaculum praebendum tauri irritarentur, ed. Orell.—

la:verb:faeneror.gloss: to lend money at interest; to practice usury
la:verb:faeneror.html:
faenĕror (less correctly fēn-, foen-), ātus sum, 1, v. dep., or (mostly post-Aug.), faenero, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
faenus
.
Prop., to lend on interest.
Form faeneror.
With abl.: pecunias istius extraordinarias grandes suo nomine faenerabatur,: primum cum posita esset pecunia apud eas societates, binis centesimis faeneratus est, took two per cent. (per month, and consequently, according to our reckoning, twenty-four per cent. per annum), , § 165.—
Absol.: a quo (Catone) cum quaereretur, quid maxime in re familiari expediret? respondit: Bene pascere ... Et cum ille, qui quaesierat, dixisset: Quid faenerari? tum Cato: Quid hominem occidere?; cf. Cato, R. R. praef. § 1.—
Form faenero.
With sub and abl.: pecuniam publicam sub usuris solitis,.—
In simple constr.: pecuniam pupillarem,.—
Without object: nil debet: faenerat immo magis,.—
Part. perf.: pecunia faenerata a tutoribus,; —
Meton.
To drain by usury: dimissiones libertorum ad faenerandas diripiendasque provincias,.—
To borrow on interest: si quis pecuniam dominicam a servo faeneratus esset,.—
To lend, impart, furnish (post-Aug. and very rare): sol suum lumen ceteris quoque sideribus faenerat,: nummos habet arca Minervae: haec sapit, haec omnes faenerat una deos,.—
Trop.
Neque enim beneficium faeneramur, practise usury with benefits, : faeneratum istuc beneficium tibi pulchre dices,i. e. richly repaid, rewarded,; cf. Ruhnk.—
Juba et Petreius mutuis

vulneribus concurrerunt et mortes faeneraverunt, exchanged with usury, i. e. inflicted on each other, .
